{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5-20251001","id":"msg_011CehYjDPxhXHEfxVUSgQbs","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Charles Babbage, a 19th-century English mathematician, conceived the first mechanical computer, the Analytical Engine, featuring an arithmetic logic unit, control flow, and memory systems. Though never completed, his designs established fundamental computing principles. In the early 20th century, mechanical calculators and tabulating machines evolved from Babbage's concepts. Herman Hollerith invented the electric tabulator in 1890, revolutionizing data processing and founding the company that became IBM. The 1930s and 1940s witnessed the emergence of sophisticated electromechanical computers like the Enigma machine and Harvard Mark I. World War II accelerated computing advancement, producing ENIAC in 1946, the first general-purpose electronic computer, employing 18,000 vacuum tubes. The transistor's invention in 1947 revolutionized computing, replacing bulky vacuum tubes with smaller, faster, more reliable components. This led to second-generation computers in the 1950s and 1960s, significantly reducing size and cost. The integrated circuit, developed in 1958, miniaturized thousands of transistors onto silicon chips, enabling third-generation computers. The microprocessor's introduction in the early 1970s, particularly the Intel 4004, transformed computing into personal devices. Apple and IBM personal computers in the 1980s brought computing into homes and offices worldwide. The graphical user interface, popularized by Xerox Alto and Apple Macintosh, made computers accessible to non-technical users. The Internet's emergence from ARPANET in 1969, combined with Tim Berners-Lee's World Wide Web development in 1989, fundamentally changed computing's purpose and reach. Mobile computing advanced dramatically through smartphones beginning with the iPhone in 2007, making computational power ubiquitous. Contemporary computing encompasses cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence, quantum computing research, and edge computing paradigms. From Babbage's mechanical gears to modern neural networks, computing's evolution reflects humanity's persistent drive to automate information processing, fundamentally reshaping society, communication, and knowledge creation."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":9,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3206,"cache_read_input_tokens":8452,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3206},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"11cf69fa-1601-436b-97b8-e7177a3897a4","uuid":"f0fb414d-1e6c-4041-994a-fc8ff5801855","request_id":"req_011CehYjCkmT2v6YeivUGoQp"}
